summary: Agriculture innovation money is flowing to tools that cut input costs on existing farms: Deere's camera sprayers (5 million acres in 2025), biological fertilizers, and gene editing now that the EU has passed light-touch rules and the US approved a PRRS-resistant pig. Venture money has fled lab-grown meat and vertical farms after billions in losses. The farm equipment cycle is at a bottom in 2026, so tech adoption is coming from retrofits and pay-per-acre models, not new machine sales.

The biggest new money in communications is AI traffic between data centers: Lumen has about $13B of AI fiber contracts and Ciena expects more than $10B of backlog, which is more certain than anything in consumer telecom. Space is the second flow: SpaceX listed in June 2026 at a target $1.75T value, Amazon is spending to catch up (Leo plus an $11.6B Globalstar deal), and satellite to phone service is moving from texting to data. Open RAN and 6G are mostly an engineering story so far; radio equipment sales are still falling.

innovations.name: AI data center interconnect (long haul fiber and coherent optics)

summary: Consumer innovation money is flowing to AI glasses and health wearables: Meta and EssilorLuxottica sold over 7 million glasses in 2025, and sales nearly doubled again in Q2 2026. Oura is going public on $1.21 billion of nine-month revenue. Cash pay health (GLP-1s through telehealth and direct from the drug maker) is the largest new consumer spend line, and AI shopping traffic is growing fast even though buying inside the chatbot has not worked yet.

innovations.name: AI glasses and personal AI devices
At-home diagnostics and continuous health sensors
Cash pay GLP-1 and protein-first nutrition

summary: Defense innovation money is moving from prototypes into first production contracts: the first ever US laser weapon production deal ($464.8 million to AeroVironment), the first drone wingman jets (General Atomics and Anduril), and up to $3.2 billion for space based interceptor prototypes. Cheap mass, meaning drones and the systems that kill drones, gets the fastest growing budgets. Many of the best positioned builders (Anduril, Castelion, Epirus, General Atomics) are private, so public exposure comes through primes, parts makers and a few volatile small caps.

innovations.name: Hypersonic strike and counter hypersonic defense

summary: The money in energy innovation is chasing firm power for AI data centers. Behind the meter fuel cells and grid batteries are already earning real revenue at scale, while advanced nuclear and enhanced geothermal have crossed from paper to construction with their first power due 2026 to 2030. Fusion is still a science bet funded by tech giants and, oddly, a merger with Trump Media.

innovations.name: Behind the meter power for data centers

summary: Financial innovation money is going into new rails for moving dollars: stablecoins (about $308B outstanding, with GENIUS Act rules taking effect January 18, 2027), tokenized securities (DTCC's tokenization service is set to launch commercially this month), and instant bank payments. The incumbents are buying their way in (Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, BlackRock, DTCC), so the clearest winners so far are the networks and asset managers, not the crypto pure plays. AI in lending and fraud is already paying off in real revenue (Upstart originations up 50%, Mastercard security services leading its fastest-growing segment).

innovations.name: Real time bank payments (FedNow, RTP, Pix, UPI)
Agentic payments (AI agents that buy for you)

summary: Most of the new money in healthcare is still going to obesity drugs: Lilly guides to $85 to $87 billion of 2026 revenue as GLP-1 volume rises 60% while prices fall. Big pharma is also buying one-time genetic medicines (Lilly bought Verve, AbbVie bought Capstan) just as the first in vivo CRISPR drug heads for FDA filing, and surgical robots now have three US rivals to Intuitive. AI diagnostics and brain implants draw heavy venture money, but reimbursement codes, not technology, are what hold them back.

innovations.name: In vivo gene editing and cell therapy
GLP-1 and next gen metabolic drugs

summary: The real money in industrials is going to automation that already pays back: warehouse robots (Symbotic backlog $22.5 billion) and industrial software and simulation (Siemens paid about $10 billion for Altair). Humanoid robots get the biggest headlines and venture checks, but they are still pilots with a few dozen to a few hundred units per site. Defense is now the main buyer pulling industrial 3D printing into real production.

innovations.name: Industrial AI software and digital twins

summary: Materials innovation money is mostly government money aimed at breaking China's hold on rare earths, magnets, gallium and graphite, with price floors, equity stakes and loans doing the work that markets will not. Two November 2026 deadlines on China's export controls are the swing factor. Battery and chip materials are the commercial frontier: sodium ion is reaching scale in China, while SiC has turned into a commodity and GaN and glass substrates ride the AI data center power shift.

innovations.name: Next generation batteries: solid state and sodium ion
New chip materials: GaN, SiC and glass substrates

summary: SpaceX's June 2026 IPO (SPCX, $75 billion raised, about $2 trillion value) made the space trade public, and nearly every other space business depends on its launch prices. The fastest real money is Starlink broadband and defense: Golden Dome and spy agencies are the main buyers of satellites, sensors and space data. Lunar landers and in space factories have real contracts and venture money but remain small, government led and slower than promised.

innovations.name: Satellite broadband and direct to phone
In space manufacturing, servicing and orbital compute

summary: Most new tech money is still AI infrastructure: about $725B of 2026 hyperscaler capex, with the fastest growth now in inference chips (Broadcom AI chip revenue up 221% y/y) and the parts that are sold out, namely advanced packaging and optics. Quantum computing moved from venture money to government money in 2026, when Commerce took equity stakes in nine firms, but revenue is still tiny. Edge AI devices ship in volume (AI PCs are over half of 2026 PC shipments) yet people rarely use the on-device AI, so that money is weaker than it looks.

innovations.name: AI inference chips and custom accelerators
Advanced packaging (CoWoS, hybrid bonding, panel level)
Edge AI devices (AI PCs, AI phones, smart glasses)

summary: Robotaxis are the one transport innovation with real scale: Waymo raised $16 billion at a $126 billion value and runs over 500,000 paid rides a week in 14 cities. Autonomous trucks, air taxis and drone delivery are funded but still pre revenue or tiny, and each waits on a regulator or a first fleet. In batteries, US EV demand fell after tax credits ended, so new cell capacity is shifting to cheaper LFP and grid storage.

innovations.name: Cheaper battery chemistries and US cell plants
